newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Sierra Leone president requests help, sanctions.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leone president requests help, sanctions.

text.p: The ousted president of Sierra Leone has requested help from West African nations to "restore democracy" after a weekend coup, the country's U.N. ambassador James Jonah said on Tuesday.

Jonah, a former U.N. undersecretary-general, told a news conference that President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah had "made an appeal (to West African countries) to help restore democracy" which could include the use of troops.

Jonah said he had been authorised to go to the forthcoming Organisation of African Unity summit in the Zimbabwean capital Harare to ask for sanctions against the coup leaders. These would include non-recognitiion of their regime and a travel ban on junior officers who organised the revolt.

Asked if Kabbah, now in Guinea, had asked for troops to overthrow the coup plotters, he said: "If possible yes, because what else do we have in the country. We have a bunch of corporals who opened the prisons wide open and 600 people came out, criminals and they are roaming the streets right now."
He said there had been a firm commitment from the West African group ECOWAS to "restore the legitimate government of Sierra Leone." But he said "how they are going to do it I do not know."

Aid workers and diplomats said Nigerian troops arrived on Monday night to reinforce Nigerians and Ghanaians of the ECOMOG regional intervention force already stationed at the airport to defend it from rebel attacks.
